# awf context

Use the lane that supplies missing evidence. Lanes are independent and may be used alone or in a useful order; none authorizes mutation or creates an effort.

<!-- awf:template-source templates/skills/context/SKILL.md.tmpl#orient -->
<!-- awf:edit orient: default; create .awf/skills/parts/context/orient.md to override -->
<!-- awf:template-source templates/skills/context/SKILL.md.tmpl -->
## Orient

Use before substantial fresh work, resume, takeover, or widened scope. Gather the applicable guidance and evidence from the current repository and, when the question requires it, other projects, dependency source or documentation, authoritative external sources, and available search tools. On resume, revalidate the whole checkpoint rather than trusting memory. State the applicable constraints, source boundaries, and remaining uncertainty. Exact-known-source reads need no skill.

<!-- awf:template-source templates/skills/context/SKILL.md.tmpl#explore -->
<!-- awf:edit explore: default; create .awf/skills/parts/context/explore.md to override -->
<!-- awf:template-source templates/skills/context/SKILL.md.tmpl -->
## Explore

Delegate one bounded unknown to the `explorer` agent only when a separate read-only investigation is useful. Give it a question, an explicit evidence boundary, and any allowed source types. Return its answer first, then evidence, uncertainty, and the boundary searched. Do not turn exploration into a workflow stage or delegate a conclusion that can be established by an exact known read.

<!-- awf:template-source templates/skills/context/SKILL.md.tmpl#challenge -->
<!-- awf:edit challenge: default; create .awf/skills/parts/context/challenge.md to override -->
<!-- awf:template-source templates/skills/context/SKILL.md.tmpl -->
## Challenge

For broad, weak, unfamiliar, or high-consequence premises, ask the `premise-checker` to try to falsify the premise. Report **supported**, **revise**, or **unresolved**, with consequence-ordered evidence. Revise the route or surface an unresolved material decision; a challenge is evidence, not approval.
